newsitem.title: USA: Treasury admits misdoings at small business program.
newsitem.headline: Treasury admits misdoings at small business program.

text.p: A top administrator at a small business program touted by President Bill Clinton wrote spurious memos to justify loans that had already been made, Treasury Department officials confirmed on Tuesday.
The department's Inspector General concluded that the administrator wrote the documents when he learned that Congress planned to review the program's files, the officials said.

The Community Development Financial Institutions Fund was touted by Clinton as a model for lending in poor areas, but it has drawn fire from Republicans who charge it made loans to institutions connected to Clinton and his wife Hillary.

House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach and other senior Republicans on the panel wrote to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Tuesday saying the memos were part of a plot to deceive a Congressional investigation into the fund's lending practices.
Treasury Department officials later confirmed to Reuters the substance of the Inspector General's report, but maintained that the fund's lending decisions were proper and not politically motivated.
